abstract: Palliative treatment of neurodegenerative diseases or organ failures includes nerve stimulators and implants. The objective of this article is to suggest a proof of concept for an alternative energy supply to batteries and thus reduce the size and increase the implantability of implants. In this paper, the wireless transfer based on guided waves in bones is studied to power deeply implanted medical devices. After selecting a material able to simulate the acoustic behavior of a bone, we first compute the associated dispersion curves to identify the most efficient guided mode to carry energy along the cortical part of a bone. We then supply energy to the source piezoelectric element using an inductive coupling operating at its resonance frequency. This first concept of hybrid energy relay thus makes it possible to consider improvements for better efficiency for implants without batteries that are difficult to access, such as inside the rib cage or in the skull.

articleTitle: Parameter Estimation of Wireless Power Transfer Systems Based on the DC Input Voltage and Current
abstract: The paper presents a parameter estimation method of wireless power transfer (WPT) systems based on the dc parameters on the primary side. The method can simultaneously realize the estimation of the mutual inductance and the output current, only using the dc input voltage and current of the inverter. Firstly, a model of a WPT system with SS compensation network is built. According to the model, the dc input current and output current are expressed by the mutual inductance, the battery voltage and the dc input voltage. Considering that the soft-start process lasts for a short time, the battery voltage is treated as a unchanged value in this process, and two groups of the dc input voltage and current are used to estimate the mutual inductance. Then, the output current is obtained based on the estimation result of the mutual inductance. Finally, A prototype of a WPT system is built and experiment are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed estimation method.

articleTitle: Impact of Design Methodologies on the Coupler Design and optimization of an Inductive Power Transfer System
abstract: Different coil structures such as circular, double D(DD), quadrature DD, bipolar, tripolar, etc., are proposed for inductive power transfer applications. Multi-objective optimization strategies are utilized to optimize these couplers to achieve objectives such as higher efficiency, lower leakage magnetic field, higher power density, lower cost, lower weight, etc. The parameters such as transmitter (Tx)-side inductance, receiver (Rx)-side inductances, and coupling coefficient (k) are constrained depending on the methodology used to design the parameters of the power electronics (PE) system. These PE system parameters are usually the voltage transfer ratio, power rating, total harmonics distortion of the transmitter and receiver current, and external quality factor. Therefore, this paper compares two design methodologies utilized to design and optimize circular couplers of a 3.7 kW IPT system. It identifies critical design equations, similarities, and differences between the two methods, and shows how some design criteria can be used to improve the IPT design process further.

articleTitle: A Novel Wireless Power Transfer System Based On ECR Coil For BCI Application
abstract: This paper proposed a novel magnetic resonance coupling system, which contains a 3D Energy concentrated rectangular (ECR) transmitter coil and a implantable coil is ECR - RWPT system. To evaluate the performance, a WPT system with external and implant coils of the same rectangular structure is designed for comparison, called the R-RWPT system. Besides, an enhancement scheme of trunk coil is proposed to increase the power transfer efficiency (PTE) with the proposed stable transfer range. The impacts of lateral and angular misalignments on the overall PTE of the systems are analyzed and compared. In the range over a center area of 20mm, and an offset angle of 20°, which is regarded as stable transmission range, the PTE is higher than 20%. Besides, the transfer loss of three system in brain tissue is considered and compared, the PTE of ECR-R-R, ECR-R, R-R WPT system can reach 27.3%, 20.5%, 14.3% at the transmission distance of 10mm separately.

articleTitle: Comparison of Shunt-Shunt and Series-Series Resonator Topology for Second-Order Inductive Power Transfer Systems
abstract: Matched inductive power transfer (IPT) transmission links with series-series and shunt-shunt resonator coupling are synthesized using filter theory. The utility of this approach is that circuit element values for the inductive resonators are easily calculated from scaled canonical filter prototypes. Using the filter theoretic context, we compare resonator inductances for series-series and shunt-shunt topologies for IPT applications operating in ISM frequency bands at 6.78 MHz, 13.56 MHz, 27.12 MHz, and 40.68 MHz. The inductance required for shunt-shunt coupling is within the nH range, while the series-series coupling has inductances in the $\mu$H range.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of a Multi-hop Resonant Wireless Power Transfer System: Optimal Intermediate Coil Size and Location
abstract: To increase the transmission distance of Wireless Power Transfer systems, engineering an intermediate coil (IC) is a common approach. In this paper, we provide methodologies and formulas for choosing the optimal size and location of an IC that provides a required transferred power to the load in a standard four-coil systems. Increasing the size of the IC will result in diminishing returns, so the optimal size depends on the target power ratio. The optimal location depends on the size of the IC and the separation of transmitting and receiving coils.

articleTitle: High Efficiency of Rectifier Circuit for WiCoPT utilizing Doubly Asymmetrical Branch-Line Coupler
abstract: In the paper, improvement of the efficiency for the Rectenna (Rectifier + Antenna) is described. The rectifier circuit in this research promotes further improvement in efficiency and expansion of the power range by using the passive path switching method that can be shifted according to the frequency band. In the previous research, the circuit was configured by using the conventional branch-line coupler as a power divider, however the conversion efficiency on the low power region was not so good. Therefore, in this research, the circuit is configured by using the doubly asymmetrical branch-line coupler to widen the impedance difference at the output ports. As a result, it was confirmed by using an electromagnetic simulation (AWR AXIEM) that the conversion efficiency at low power region was improved up to 65.8%, which was about twice that of the conventional one. In addition, it is verified experimentally as well as analyzed.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of a 30 kW Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer System for Electric Vehicle
abstract: The present work aims at quantifying how the position of the receiver in a realistic dynamic wireless power transfer (DWPT) system affects the transmission process for electric vehicles. With the aim of considering the transmitted power, the position of the receiver is influenced by the factors that are the moving distance along the X axis, the misalignment along the Y axis, the vertical variation along the Z axis and the rotation angle along the Z axis. The analysis is based on the polynomial chaos expansions for a low computational cost and a fast sensitivity analysis.

articleTitle: Numerical Calculation of the AC Resistance in a Litz Wire Applying the MTL Theory
abstract: The performance of a Litz wire for wireless power transfer (WPT) applications is investigated by a new prediction model. The litz wire composed of many insulated strands is assumed to be a multiconductor transmission line (MTL). The MTL impedance and admittance matrices are extracted respectively from a numerical solution of electrostatic and eddy current equations. The variable position of the strands in the cross section of the wire is taken into account to evaluate the electrical performance in terms of the AC resistance. Different litz cable configurations are analyzed at different frequencies and the ratio between AC resistance and DC resistance is predicted.

articleTitle: Distributed Ambient SWIPT System
abstract: This article demonstrates the great utility of distributed approaches in backscattered communication systems. Initially, the distributed network, composed of backscatter transmitters and receivers is demonstrated. Then this is combined with an RF-DC converter and a fully Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer (SWIPT) is described in detail. Combining these two technologies demonstrates that it is possible to reuse a city’s 5G network as a gateway for smart city monitoring without increasing the current radiation level or energy consumption.

Author Keywords: Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer (SWIPT)

articleTitle: Reducing and Validating Surface Flux Emissions for High-Power Wireless Charging Systems
abstract: This paper investigates methods of reducing surface flux in high-power inductive power transfer (IPT) magnetics used for wireless charging electric vehicles (EVs) and identifies sources of error between simulated and measured surface flux data. Existing IPT literature analyses leakage flux for low and high-power IPT systems, but rarely considers surface flux emissions from the ground assembly (GA) magnetics. In this work, simulations are used to identify relationships between magnetic design geometry, surface flux, and leakage flux. Recommendations are made that reduce surface flux in high-power IPT systems considering the needs of foreign object detection (FOD) systems. Experiments are performed using a 50 kW system to identify sources of error between simulated and measured surface flux and leakage flux. Further recommendations are made regarding accurately measuring surface flux maximums on candidate magnetics. A demonstration of the 50 kW system referenced in this work can be found at: https://dx.doi.org/10.21227/e2tf5095

articleTitle: Wireless Power Charging and Motion Control of a Magnetic Robot
abstract: Numerous studies on magnetic robots at the millimeter or micrometer-scale have focused on motion control and a few other functions such as surveillance or object pickup and drop-off. However, with these basic functions only, magnetic robots are still far from their true potential. More complex functions could be achieved with a powerful and intense energy source, which is difficult to implement with their small size. In this paper, a new magnetic robot topology, based on the conventional permanent magnet synchronous motor, is proposed. It features at the same time a motion control solution and a wireless charging solution that reduces the dependency of the robot on its power source. The multi-physics modeling of the robot and the magnetic platform is presented. Then, the simulated results are analyzed.

articleTitle: Distributed Excitation of a Birdcage Transmitter for Wireless Powering of Endoscopic Capsules
abstract: This study deals with an innovative design of the excitation system of a birdcage transmitter for wireless powering of micro implants. The use of the birdcage coil is a very promising solution to realize an efficient transmitting system. This type of source, widely used for the magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), ensures a circularly polarized magnetic field inside the human body. One of the main issues is the excitation system of the birdcage coil as the field is highly sensitive to small variations in the coil geometry. The idea is to replace the traditional birdcage with a geometrically deformed cage that can be installed on a wearable corset, adaptable to different body shapes while maintaining electromagnetic functionality. Thus, an innovative system is presented with independent feeding for each leg of the cage. The robustness of the proposed solution is tested varying the birdcage coil geometry assuming a working frequency of 300 kHz.

articleTitle: Three-Phase Asymmetric Phase Modulation for Inductive Power Transfer Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the use of Three-Phase Asymmetric Phase modulation for three-phase IPT systems utilising a standard six-switch inverter. This modulation scheme is mathematically described and is compared to the output voltage modulation schemes that are typically used in three-phase IPT systems. An IPT system with a delta connected, LCL-LCL compensation network and a passive three-phase secondary is considered as an example in this paper to show that the proposed asymmetric modulation scheme can significantly lower switching losses.

articleTitle: Appropriate Conventional Rectifier Topology for Low-Power RF Energy Harvesting
abstract: This article presents a comparative study among commonly used rectifier topologies in literature. The goal of this comparison is to emphasize on advantages and drawbacks of each topology and to see which is the best candidate for low power RF energy harvesting. Comparison is first made in simulation with source-pull optimization techniques in order to find the best behaviour of each topology for a given frequency, RF input power and load. The results are then validated by measurements, to confirm simulation results and draw valid conclusions.

articleTitle: Optimizing RF-DC Converters Input Impedance Selection
abstract: This paper explores the optimization of RF-DC converters, focusing on the impacts of the input power on the design of the impedance matching networks. In order to implement this analysis, a source pull simulation was performed, and two circuits were designed to compare its behaviours. This analysis made it possible to conclude that when using a voltage multiplier as the RF-DC solution, the diode requires high reactance at the source for low input power values but for high input powers, the diode requires an impedance approaching a very low impedance. Both high and low input power circuits achieved approximately 40 % efficiency.

articleTitle: Determination Method of Target Material and Coil Area Based on Average Magnetic Flux Density for Metal Object Detection of Dynamic WPT
abstract: The detection of foreign metal objects is an essential technology to ensure the safety of the wireless power transfer (WPT) systems. The standards of required detection targets and areas have already been proposed for the static WPT (S-WPT) system. However, for the dynamic WPT (D-WPT) system, it is necessary to take into account that the magnetic field varies with the position of the receiver coil. This paper proposes a method to determine the detection targets and area for the D-WPT system. First, the average of the magnetic flux density during one charge in D-WPT is calculated using an electromagnetic field simulator. Next, the average magnetic flux density is applied to various metal plates using the S-WPT test bench, and its temperature is observed. The applying period is the same as the D-WPT driving situation. Finally, the magnetic flux density at the point when the saturation temperature of each metal reaches $80^{\circ}\text{C}$ is used as the threshold value, and the required detection area is determined by comparing it with the average magnetic flux density distribution. The proposal was experimentally verified using our developed WPT system, whose rated power is 20 kW. This proposal is helpful because the test can be conducted without moving the receiver coil, and can clearly define the required detection target and area for the foreign metal objects in the D-WPT system.

articleTitle: mm-Wave Polarization Insensitive Spiral Antenna for 5G Energy Harvesting Applications
abstract: This paper presents the development of a dual-band antenna for novel RF Energy Harvesting and Wireless Power Transfer systems operating on the fifth-generation (5G) cellular networks frequencies. A logarithmic spiral is selected to provide circular polarization in 5G bands. A conformal balun is designed to ensure a symmetric excitation of the spirals’ arms. A ring reflector is proposed to ascertain the stable gain (>5dBic) and axial ratio (<3db) in the 20 and 40 GHz frequency bands after the spiral and the balun were integrated. A ring reflector for realised gain improvement is implemented. The internal radius, external radius and thickness of the ring were optimised to provide additional gain over the desired frequencies without noticeable deterioration of the axial ratio.

articleTitle: Investigation of Transmission Efficiency on Short-range 4x4 MIMO WiCoPT System
abstract: This research has investigated the short-range Multi Input Multi Output (MIMO) Wireless Communication and Power Transfer (WiCoPT) system that can simultaneously transmit information and power using the same antenna and frequency band. A 4x4 MIMO system with 2x2 planar patch antennas is used for both transmission and reception. The previous work indicated the proposed WiCoPT system can achieve high-level transmission capacity and power transmission efficiency. In addition, the system significantly improved the positioning-free capability. This paper demonstrates the measured performances and investigates the relationship between the input and output feeding circuits (matching circuits) and the transmission efficiency. The investigation clarifies there is an optimal matching condition to maximize the transmission efficiency under the MIMO control. The maximum efficiency improvement of 35 points is achieved at a transmission distance of 10 mm, with a transmission efficiency of 59%, and the corresponding maximum transmission capacity of 52 bit/s/Hz. These results promise that a variable matching circuit will effectively optimize the propagation condition between the transmitter and the receiver under the MIMO control, resulting in high-level transmission characteristics.

articleTitle: Magnetic and Coupling approach to optimizing Inductive Power Transfer Systems
abstract: This paper presents a comparison of two methods of geometric optimization of wireless power transmission systems: adjustment of the coupling coefficient and obtaining a uniform magnetic field. 4 types of calculations were carried out (with a change in the resistance of the transmitting and receiving boards, size of the transmitting coil and case with pairs of identical coils). optimization by obtaining a uniform field in some cases allowed obtaining a system that is tolerant to displacements and with smaller coil sizes. However, the coupling coefficient adjustment method proved to be more reliable and provided the required energy transfer stability in all cases.

articleTitle: Highly Efficient 900 MHz Minkowski Rectenna for RF Energy Harvesting Applications
abstract: The compact rectifying antenna (rectenna) proposed in this presentation consists in a 1st iteration fractal Minkowski loop antenna associated with rectifying circuit. The loop antenna has been simulated and optimized. It occupies the perimeter of 0.74 wavelength at the operating frequency of 900 MHz. The reflection coefficient is about -26dB at 900 MHz. The antenna had a realized gain of2 dBi and a transfer function of 0.08 m. It also presents an efficiency of 91%. The rectifying circuits are composed of a low threshold single series diode, one capacitor and a single load. This single load is a 10 $\mathrm{k}\Omega$ resistor, which represents the input impedance of the DC-DC boost charger. The whole rectenna has been simulated and it presents 55% as the RF-DC conversion efficiency for a power density of 1 uW/cm2.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Supply of Moving Linear Actuator Enclosed in Stainless-Steel
abstract: Linear actuators are a key element of automatized industrial systems, as linear motion is present in most manipulation tasks. For actuators performing x-z movements, actuator windings are placed on the moving part and these must be supplied. However, in high-purity environments such as in the food processing or pharmaceutical industries, actuators should be fully enclosed in stainless steel (SS) to facilitate thorough cleaning, and cables are undesirable. This paper therefore proposes high-efficiency (97% at 100W) wireless power transfer (WPT) through two 0.5mm thick SS enclosures, which facilitates the deployment of linear actuators in high-purity environments. The proposed coaxial transformer arrangement with the magnetic core mounted on the moving part results in a magnetic field that is in parallel to the SS enclosures, which minimizes eddy-current losses. We discuss the detailed modeling and optimization of the system, and finally present an industrial two-axis actuator prototype that fully confirms the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Eigenvalue Distortion in a Double-Sided LCC-Compensated Stationary Automotive WPT System during Coil Alignment
abstract: Due to lateral coil misalignment in automotive wireless power transfer (WPT) systems, its eigen-frequencies are inherently distorted. This paper contributes to the fundamental analysis of resonant tank detuning in doubled-sided LCC-compensated stationary automotive WPT systems during the coil alignment prior to charging. Therefore, the system’s input impedance is analyzed in the complex frequency domain in terms of its poles and zeros. A reference design from the latest SAE J2954 standard is simulated in a Finite-Element-Analysis to account for the positioning dependency of the coupled coils system. For a double-sided LCC-compensated WPT system, the impedance behavior at the input and output terminals of the circuit is then characterized by means of a First Harmonic Approximation (FHA). Through this, system characteristics useful for further investigations concerning VA positioning feedback are revealed.

articleTitle: Limitations of Ansys-Maxwell and Simplorer Magnetostatic co-simulation in Inductive Wireless Power Transfer
abstract: The popularity gained by wireless power transfer (WPT) in recent years for low and high-power electronics challenged researchers to develop novel systems tackling the rising demand for wirelessly charged devices. In this process, simulation softwares have been used as a tool for validating theoretical models or concepts. The electromagnetic-package offered by Ansys, specifically Maxwell and Simplorer are amongst the most commonly used ones. This article discusses the limitations of Maxwell and Simplorer magnetostatic co-simulation in modelling an inductive WPT system using a simple topology, i.e. inductively coupled transmitter-receiver coils. Its performance with both horizontal coil misalignment and vertical coil separation for all three working regions: over-coupled, coupled and loosely-coupled was investigated in both simulation and experiment. The simulation and experimental results are compared to highlight the areas in which the simulation software can have limitations, e.g.: inaccurately predicting the maximum simulated efficiency in over-coupled and loosely-coupled areas when compared with the experiment.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Compensated Wireless Power Transfer System with Quasi-Constant Output Power against Load Variations
abstract: This paper proposed a new hybrid compensated wireless power system that provides a relatively constant output power profile under the load variation situation. Two different frequency selective compensation networks are developed for the characteristic combination of series-series and series-parallel compensation networks. By utilizing the fundamental and third harmonic voltage components of the phase-shift-controlled inverter, the proposed system could simultaneously exhibit both output characteristics of constant current and constant voltage at different frequencies. Based on the compensative effect against the load variation, the output power can be maintained almost constant at a certain load range. The theoretical analysis proves the feasibility of the proposed system with the support of the Superposition Theorem. A down-size prototype is developed for verification. The experimental results show that the system achieves an approximately constant output power of 40W when the load varies from 20 to $65 \Omega$ with a maximum power fluctuation of 4.76%.

articleTitle: Battery-free, Wirelessly Powered and Controlled Concrete Resistivity Sensing Node
abstract: This paper presents a generic Sensing Node, part of a Cyber-Physical System, dedicated to the Structural Health Monitoring of reinforced concretes. The Sensing Node is: battery-free; low-power; fully wireless; wirelessly, remotely and omnidirectionally powered and controlled by the Communicating Node(s) over several meters (at least 11 meters in indoor). It can be buried in the reinforced concrete and measure relevant parameters, such as temperature, relative humidity, mechanical deformation, and electrical resistivity to estimate the corrosion rate. By using a unique antenna, the proposed solution meets the requirements of the Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer paradigm. The proposed system is easily scalable to other applications, especially in harsh environments.

Author Keywords: Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer (SWIPT)
